slots.supply_status: Component supply is tight across the board: lead times are stretching and MOSFETs in particular are short, though Delta's purchasing scale and supplier relationships keep demand largely fulfilled. Memory was the hardest hit - one business unit could not secure memory volumes at workable prices, so it switched designs to second sources and expects H2 shipments to normalize and catch up the backlog without a loss. Management does not expect power semiconductors to repeat memory's shortage dynamics - the two situations differ a lot - but notes power-semi supply is cyclical because capacity investment takes long. On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.

concentration.text: Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center and Generate announced on October 1, 2026 that the first patient has been dosed in the first-in-human Phase 1 trial (NCT07489287) of GB-5267, an investigational autologous IL-18 armored CAR T-cell therapy targeting MUC16 (over-expressed by more than 80% of ovarian tumors), in ovarian cancer, recruiting patients whose disease has returned after treatment or does not respond to platinum-based chemotherapy, the standard first-line treatment; the trial, led by Principal Investigator Emese Zsiros at Roswell Park, evaluates safety and tolerability and is enrolling. Each patient's T cells are collected, genetically engineered and expanded in Roswell Park's GMP Engineering & Cell Manufacturing Facility. The study requires no lymphodepletion chemotherapy and delivers the cells both intravenously and into the peritoneal cavity. Generate engineered GB-5267 with AI by designing and evaluating CAR architectures at scale based on how T cells actually behave rather than on binding affinity, optimizing potency, proliferation and persistence; the release calls it the first next-generation cell therapy for ovarian cancer to enter clinical trials (company claim). concentration.text: Malta model and timeline (investor webinar): a special purpose vehicle owned by the U.S. and Japanese governments funds and owns the fab infrastructure, tooling and operating expenses and receives the wafer revenue; GF builds and operates the fabs, provides its technology (including FDX, UX and BCD) and manages operating expenses, and earns technology, construction and operating management fees plus EBITDA sharing and shared-services reimbursement (technology fees commence in 2027 and run for a minimum of 20 years). Phase 1 and Phase 2 together are up to ~1.8M wafers/yr (300mm-equivalent, ~900k per phase at full run rate; the Phase 2 fab is subject to approval), with 1,000+ high-skilled manufacturing jobs. On GF's illustrative timeline Phase 1 is ready for equipment in 2028, has its first wafer out in 2029 and reaches baseline capacity in 2031, and Phase 2 has its first wafer out in 2031 (page 9 chart). Renesas CEO Hidetoshi Shibata is quoted in the deck: 'We are planning around GF's new capacity in New York as an extension of Renesas‘ own production footprint'. — up to ~1.8M wafers/yr for Phase 1 + 2; Phase 1 first wafer out 2029 (page 9 chart)

concentration.text: Customer: Mizuho Securities selected HPE Cray XD2000 featuring direct liquid cooling and will build a new direct-liquid-cooling-ready data center for it, to run financial simulations (derivatives pricing, market risk and counterparty credit risk) involving more than 360 million calculations per day. Installation of the liquid cooling equipment, system buildout and operational validation begin this fall, with the system scheduled to go into production in mid-2027. The initial deployment comprises eight server nodes, with Mizuho Securities planning to expand servers and racks in stages; it plans to validate direct liquid cooling through this system as it explores GPU-accelerated compute for its future private AI infrastructure. Per HPE, direct liquid cooling in this configuration delivers up to 20% performance improvement per kilowatt over air-cooled solutions and consumes 15% less power, and Mizuho Securities expects 1.6 times the performance per server node versus its current environment. HPE Services will provide monitoring and maintenance including real-time visibility into the direct liquid cooling and power infrastructure and automated coolant leak alerts. Hirokazu Mochizuki, SVP and managing director for HPE Japan, calls Mizuho Securities the first in Japan's financial sector to select HPE Cray XD2000 featuring direct liquid cooling. concentration.text: LS Eco Energy is investing KRW 11.6 billion to build a samarium metal production facility of about 240 tons a year at its LSCV site in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and plans trial mass production in December; the company says the volume is enough for about 700-1,000 tons a year of SmCo (samarium-cobalt) permanent magnets, used mainly in fighter jets and missiles, and calls it the first defense rare-earth metal production base outside China (company claim). It cites the US extending Defense Department supply-chain rules for SmCo magnets to the raw-material stage from January 2027. The release describes the structure as the first commercialisation of the Lynas cooperation: Lynas Rare Earths supplies the rare-earth feedstock, LS Eco Energy produces the metal in Vietnam and supplies it to LS Cable & System's permanent-magnet plant. The company plans to extend rare-earth metal production to dysprosium (Dy), terbium (Tb) and NdPr. — KRW 11.6 billion investment; about 240 tons a year samarium metal; trial mass production in December

Lam saw 'a little bit of tightness' in its supply chain in the quarter, which held back the December guide; it is working with suppliers to accelerate their capacity expansion and hosted 'a couple of big events' with its global suppliers in the last two months. CEO: 'this is nothing like' the COVID shortages; some suppliers, for example in advanced packaging, see Lam's demand on them rising much faster than Lam itself, and 'we'll be caught up very shortly'. CFO: Lam would be open to investing in suppliers if needed but many are well capitalized, and it is building inventory for next year's demand.

slots.guidance: Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): October shipments are about the same as September and November should start to decline; the customer cut its forecast in September, which management reads as the new phone series not selling well, and customers give no long forecast. Green power is a structural cost because customer contracts require Largan to buy it in proportion to that customer's share; next year's prices are already negotiated, so it can be reflected in prices only the year after. Yield on the new variable-aperture lens now looks OK, and utilization should be full in Q4.
slots.supply_status: Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): FA and FAU are the CPO parts in shortest supply, and customers want Largan to build as much capacity as it can; replicating the lines may require outsourcing some capacity because Largan's own may not be enough, while its FA / FAU alignment equipment is built in-house. All the land recently bought has a clear use, for cleanroom production lines, existing buildings will be demolished and rebuilt, and lines started next year will be completed in 2030, all planned for FAU rather than smartphone lenses.
slots.next_catalyst: Management (Q&A answers, speakers unlabeled): Largan's fiber array (FA) certification with its customer 'should count as passed', with one customer for volume production; the customer now wants complete FAUs, so Largan will make the FA, buy in PMLA and other parts and couple them into FAUs, and seeks to mount the FAU on the carrier too, acting for this generation like a contractor. The FA pilot line is ready and the customer has visited many times; a newly completed plant will be used entirely for FAU, with lines built by mid next year, and management confirmed ('should be right') that FAU volume production can start in the second half of 2027, the product looking like 'FAU plus carrier' with the carrier board and balls bought in. Multi-row FA is at the sampling stage, for 2028 projects at the earliest and not visible next year, with direct end-customer contact so far only on that next generation; grating-coupling products go to volume production next year while edge coupling is in co-work. FA and FAU are the scarcest CPO parts now; for FAUs, NPO versus CPO makes little difference.

concentration.role: customer (design win: SiC hybrid power modules for PowerTitan 3.0 BESS)
concentration.text: Design win (onsemi's word): Sungrow has adopted onsemi's latest EliteSiC silicon carbide hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 utility-scale battery energy storage (BESS) platform, which incorporates onsemi's high-density power integrated modules (PIMs) optimized for three-level inverter architectures. Versus the previous-generation platform the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW and peak efficiency exceeding 99.3%. According to onsemi analysis, the 0.4% improvement could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW BESS installation compared with the previous-generation module. The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship; the companies collaborated through platform definition, system optimization and qualification. Sergio Fissore, VP and GM, IPD Power Division: the EliteSiC hybrid power module 'enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems'. — inverter-level efficiency +0.4%; PCUs up to 450 kW; peak efficiency exceeding 99.3%; more than 475 MWh saved annually per 100 MW (onsemi analysis)
